item.title: What Is PostgreSQL? A Quick Review
item.description:
PostgreSQL, often referred to as Postgres, is a powerful, open-source relational database management system (RDBMS). Known for its reliability, robustness, and feature set, PostgreSQL is widely used for managing structured data in applications ranging from web development to data analytics.

First released in 1986 and continuously improved, PostgreSQL is now a leading choice for developers and organizations looking for an advanced database solution that prioritizes scalability and compliance with SQL standards.

item.title: Solved: How-to-Generate-UUID-in-PostgreSQL
item.description:
Solved: How-to-Generate-UUID-in-PostgreSQL

Summary:
In PostgreSQL, UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) is often used for unique identifiers in databases. However, creating these identifiers varies between different PostgreSQL versions. This guide will cover multiple methods, including using extensions and functions like gen_random_uuid() and uuid_generate_v4() for generating UUIDs. You’ll also find practical examples, detailed code explanations, and alternatives for older versions of PostgreSQL.

What is a UUID and Why Should You Use It?

UUIDs are 128-bit values that provide a unique identifier that can be used in your database. Unlike traditional integer-based primary keys, UUIDs offer a larger address space and are useful in distributed systems where it’s important to prevent identifier collisions.

item.title: Chinook Database - PostgreSQL Sample Database
item.description:
PostgreSQL is one of the most popular relational database management systems used today. One of the benefits of PostgreSQL is its ability to handle complex data structures, which makes it an ideal choice for managing large-scale databases. In this blog post, we’ll take a closer look at the sample database of PostgreSQL , the Chinook database, which is widely used for educational and training purposes.

The Chinook database is a postgresql sample database that contains information about a music store. It is designed to demonstrate various features of PostgreSQL, including data modeling, query optimization, and performance tuning. The database consists of eleven tables, each of which is related to the others through primary and foreign keys.
